content: The analysis of patients with genotype 1 infection, as well as those with an unknown or mixed genotype population, revealed that 95% of patients achieved sustained virologic response at 12 weeks (SVR12) in both genotype subgroups. The GRADE assessments for these outcomes ranged from low to high. In the all-treatment experience analysis of patients treated with glecaprevir and pibrentasvir, evidence was available across all genotypes. The percentage of patients achieving SVR12 ranged from 83% to 98%, with GRADE assessments varying from very low to high. For treatment-naïve patients treated with glecaprevir and pibrentasvir, evidence was available only for those with genotype 3 infection (N=419). The SVR12 rate was 95%, with a GRADE assessment of high. In treatment-experienced patients treated with glecaprevir and pibrentasvir, evidence was available only for those with genotype 3 infection (N=24). The SVR12 rate was 92%, with a GRADE assessment of very low. For patients treated with ledipasvir and sofosbuvir, evidence was available across all genotypes. The SVR12 rates ranged from 64% to 98%, with GRADE assessments varying from very low to high. In treatment-naïve patients treated with ledipasvir and sofosbuvir, evidence was available for genotypes 1, 3-5, and mixed or unknown genotypes. The SVR12 rates ranged from 64% to 98%, with GRADE assessments varying from very low to high. In treatment-experienced patients treated with ledipasvir and sofosbuvir, evidence was available for genotypes 1, 4-6, and mixed or unknown genotypes. The SVR12 rates ranged from 87% to 97%, with GRADE assessments varying from very low to high. For patients treated with paritaprevir/ritonavir, ombitasvir, and dasabuvir, evidence was available only for genotype 1 infection. The SVR12 rates ranged from 98% to 99%, with GRADE assessments of high. In treatment-naïve patients treated with paritaprevir/ritonavir, ombitasvir, and dasabuvir, evidence was available only for genotype 1 infection. The SVR12 rates ranged from 97% to 98%, with GRADE assessments of high. For patients treated with sofosbuvir and velpatasvir, evidence was available across all genotypes. The SVR12 rates ranged from 89% to 99%, with GRADE assessments varying from low to high. In treatment-naïve patients treated with sofosbuvir and velpatasvir, evidence was available for genotypes 1-3 and mixed or unknown genotypes. The SVR12 rates ranged from 84% to 98%, with GRADE assessments varying from very low to high. In treatment-experienced patients treated with sofosbuvir and velpatasvir, evidence was available for genotypes 1-3. The SVR12 rates ranged from 85% to 97%, with GRADE assessments varying from low to high. For patients treated with sofosbuvir, velpatasvir, and voxilaprevir, evidence was available across all genotypes. The SVR12 rates ranged from 81% to 98%, with GRADE assessments varying from very low to high. In treatment-naïve patients treated with sofosbuvir, velpatasvir, and voxilaprevir, evidence was available only for genotype 3 infection. The SVR12 rate was 96%, with a GRADE assessment of high. In treatment-experienced patients treated with sofosbuvir, velpatasvir, and voxilaprevir, evidence was available across all genotypes. The SVR12 rates ranged from 75% to 98%, with GRADE assessments varying from very low to high. For patients treated with daclatasvir and asunaprevir, evidence was available for genotype 1 infection and mixed or unknown genotypes. The SVR12 rates ranged from 89% to 90%, with GRADE assessments varying from very low to high. In treatment-naïve patients treated with daclatasvir and asunaprevir, evidence was available only for genotype 1 infection. The pooled SVR12 rate was 91%, with a GRADE assessment of moderate. In treatment-experienced patients treated with daclatasvir and asunaprevir, evidence was available only for genotype 1 infection. The pooled SVR12 rate was 83%, with a GRADE assessment of moderate. For patients treated with daclatasvir and sofosbuvir, evidence was available for genotypes 1-3, 5, and 6, as well as mixed or unknown genotypes. The SVR12 rates ranged from 63% to 96%, with GRADE assessments varying from very low to low. In treatment-naïve patients treated with daclatasvir and sofosbuvir, evidence was available only for genotype 3 infection. The SVR12 rates ranged from 58% to 65%, with GRADE assessments of very low. In treatment-experienced patients treated with daclatasvir and sofosbuvir, evidence was available for genotypes 1 and 3. The SVR12 rates ranged from 69% to 98%, with GRADE assessments varying from very low to low. For patients treated with elbasvir and grazoprevir, evidence was available for genotype 1 infection and mixed or unknown genotypes. The SVR12 rates ranged from 96% to 97%, with GRADE assessments varying from moderate to high. In treatment-naïve patients treated with elbasvir and grazoprevir, evidence was available for genotype 1 infection and mixed or unknown genotypes. The SVR12 rates ranged from 95% to 98%, with GRADE assessments varying from low to high. In treatment-experienced patients treated with elbasvir and grazoprevir, evidence was available for genotype 1 infection and mixed or unknown genotypes. The SVR12 rates ranged from 95% to 98%, with GRADE assessments varying from low to high.
